info.text:
No federal law requires your job to pay severance.

The US Labor Department says severance is a matter of agreement. One related rule: the WARN Act, 60 days' notice or back pay for mass layoffs at firms with 100+ workers.
The IRS treats severance as supplemental wages: employers can withhold a flat 22% federal. Hypothetical: 10 weeks on a $60,000 salary = $11,538, about $2,538 withheld.
Workers 40+ get 21 days to consider an age-claim release (45 in group layoffs) and 7 days to revoke.
Announced US job cuts hit 1,206,374 in 2025 (Challenger, Gray & Christmas).

Sources: US Dept. of Labor; IRS Pub 15 (2026); EEOC; Challenger, Gray & Christmas.
Some states, like New Jersey, require severance in certain mass layoffs.
News and education, not legal or financial advice.
